name: General Medicine
overview: The first two years are theory: medical chemistry, biophysics, cell and molecular biology, anatomy, histology, embryology and physiology. Year three moves to pathology, pathophysiology, microbiology and immunology, with hands-on work that includes anatomical and pathological autopsies. In years four and five you rotate through the clinical disciplines in small groups, while ethics and medical psychology run alongside. The final year is an internship across internal medicine, surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, neurology, psychiatry and family medicine, with a thesis and state exams at the end. Graduates go on to specialist training, doctoral research, or work in hospitals, public health and health administration.

name: Dentistry
overview: Basic sciences and general medical knowledge are taught in the departments and clinics of the partner faculties, with dental subjects appearing early and taking up more of the timetable from the third year on. Teaching happens in small-group practicals led by close to sixty dentists, so you build independent clinical skills before graduating. Four summer practices cover the dental laboratory, dental assistance, dento-alveolar work and general dentistry. A thesis is part of the degree. Graduates can start practising dentistry or move into specialist or PhD training.

name: Pharmaceutical Sciences
overview: The first two years rest on chemistry, biology, mathematics and physics, taught through both lectures and laboratory classes. Pharmacy-specific subjects arrive in years two and three, with a high share of practical training and several internships. Work on the diploma thesis begins in the fourth year, and the degree ends with a compulsory practice period, thesis submission and a final exam. Teaching draws on a large clinical base for bedside pharmacy training. Graduates work in pharmaceutical research, industry, regulatory authorities and the pharmaceutical trade across the EU, and the science grounding also opens related fields such as chemistry, bioengineering and biology.

name: Nursing
overview: The first year is built on health-science basics such as anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, and public health and epidemiology, followed by nursing theory and practice. You learn in small groups with a mentor, and clinical practice under tutor supervision runs through the degree. The fourth year is mostly field placements and the thesis. You can focus on areas such as internal medicine, surgery, obstetrics-gynaecology, intensive therapy, paediatrics, neurology, psychiatry, primary care and oncology. Graduates work in primary care, hospital wards, nursing homes and hospices, or continue to a master's.

name: Midwifery
overview: Year one covers health-science foundations: anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, public health and epidemiology. Later years bring midwifery subjects including obstetrics-gynaecology, neonatal and paediatric medicine and nursing, perioperative care, the psychology of supportive connection and ethics in midwifery. Small classes, a mentor system and a high-fidelity birthing simulator prepare you for supervised clinical placements, and the fourth year is mainly field practice and the thesis. Graduates work in delivery rooms, prenatal and postpartum care, outpatient departments, lactation consulting and family planning, or go on to a master's.

name: Dietetics
overview: After a first year of health-science basics, you study food science, meal preparation technology, nutrition science, public health nutrition, clinical dietetics, catering management and food hygiene. Small-group teaching with a mentor includes cooking practice in teaching kitchens, and you train in clinics and food-production plants under tutor supervision. The fourth year is given to field placements and a thesis that you defend before graduating. Graduates work as nutrition experts in hospitals and care institutions, as nutrition advisers, or in catering, fitness and wellness and health promotion, and can continue to a master's.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: The first year covers health-science basics including anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, oncology and public health. You then study the functional analysis of the musculoskeletal system, electrotherapy, cardiorespiratory and internal-medicine physiotherapy, orthopaedic and neurological work, and physiotherapy for specific age groups including children. Small classes, a mentor system and well-equipped skill labs support the practical side, with clinical placements throughout and extended fieldwork and a thesis in year four. Graduates work in hospitals, clinics, rehabilitation centres, sports medicine, home care and wellness, or progress to the physiotherapy master's.

name: Medical Diagnostic Analysis (Optometry)
overview: After a first year of anatomy, physiology and other health-science basics, optometry content takes over: ocular anatomy, ophthalmic pathology and optics, contact lenses, clinical ophthalmology, binocular vision, ophthalmic technology and paediatric ophthalmology. Teaching is in small groups with a mentor, and clinical practice builds up to field placements and a thesis in the fourth year. The diploma records the optometry specialisation. Graduates work in optical shops, outpatient eye clinics and hospitals, diagnostic laboratories and optical-product management, and can continue to a master's.

name: Public Health Supervisor
overview: You begin with anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology and microbiology, then move into applied chemistry, toxicology, public health engineering, environmental health, food hygiene and safety, epidemiology and prevention of communicable diseases, occupational health, chemical safety and radiation health. Training in clinics and public health institutions is practice-oriented and supervised by tutors, and the fourth year is field practice and a thesis defended at the end. Graduates work in regional public health administration, hospital hygiene, industrial and agricultural inspection, multinational companies, health insurance, occupational health and health promotion, or continue to a master's.

name: Health Care Management with Health Tourism Specialisation
overview: Health-science foundations such as anatomy, physiology and preventive medicine sit beside leisure and tourism studies, health tourism products and medical tourism. Later modules cover health destination development, experience and service design, sales and marketing in health tourism, spa management and event management, along with quality management, project management and online communication. Small-group teaching with mentor support leads to a final semester of field practice and the thesis. Graduates work with health service providers, tour operators, health resorts, sanatoria, private healthcare providers, spas and thermal baths.

name: Conductive Education
overview: The degree combines social, medical and pedagogical sciences: pedagogy, psychology, IT, a foreign language and conductive pedagogy in year one, then neurology, communication and medical biology, with legal and ethical aspects and rehabilitation in the last year. Practice classes start in the first week, and in the final year nearly every second class is practice with real children, using the faculty's own practice areas. In the second year you choose nursery school education, primary school education or pedagogical rehabilitation. Graduates work as conductor teachers in multi-professional education, rehabilitation or health settings, including adult rehabilitation for conditions such as Parkinson's disease.

name: Vehicle Engineering
overview: The curriculum is built from natural sciences, economics and human sciences, a large block of vehicle-engineering professional subjects, optional electives and a thesis course. Graduates find work in the design and manufacture of vehicles, including at Audi and its suppliers, as well as in vehicle maintenance and operation at transport companies such as Volan, BKV and MAV, at transport authorities and brand service centres. Some set up their own supplier or consulting businesses, and the degree prepares you for a master's.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The programme gives you a broad grounding in engineering disciplines together with solid skills in mechanical engineering, including experimenting with systems and interpreting the data. Graduates work in the design and manufacture of machines at employers such as Audi and its suppliers, Bosch, Nemak and Dana, in vehicle operation and maintenance at transport companies, in industrial automation, at authorities and service centres, or in their own supplier and consulting firms. Some move into management roles, and the degree prepares you for a master's.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: The degree combines natural sciences, economics and human sciences, fundamental and specialised technical subjects, and a thesis course. As a civil engineer you work with architects, contractors, government officials and finance specialists. Graduates go into engineering design, construction management, government regulatory agencies, field and laboratory testing, operation and maintenance of civil works, site planning, contract oversight, project management and facilities management. The bachelor's also prepares you for a master's.

name: Logistics Engineering
overview: The curriculum combines natural sciences, economics and human sciences, a large block of professional logistics subjects and a thesis course, giving you technical expertise alongside an understanding of business principles. You learn to design experiments, analyse and interpret data, and apply the results to how goods and materials move. Graduates work as logistics managers, supply chain analysts, operations managers, transportation planners, warehouse managers, consultants or entrepreneurs, and can continue to a master's.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: The first four semesters cover the foundations of electrical engineering, and the last three are devoted to one of two specialisations, Automation or Infocommunications, though you may take electives from either. The programme is taught project by project, giving you insight into industrial projects while you study. Infocommunications graduates work as network planners, system integrators or IT security experts, and Automation graduates as robotics engineers, PLC programmers, automation system designers or operators of manufacturing systems. Other paths include sensor development, data processing, the energy sector and smart-city solutions.

name: Business Informatics
overview: You study business processes alongside information systems architecture, computing infrastructure, databases, programming, IT regulation and information management, which takes in IT strategy, project and knowledge management, IT security and IT audit. The degree ends with a thesis. Graduates work as business analysts and in IT project management, software development, database management, digitalisation, IT consultancy and business intelligence, or in systems engineering and systems analysis.

name: Agricultural Engineering
overview: The first semesters rest on chemistry, plant and animal physiology, physics and mathematics. From the third semester the focus turns to animal breeding and crop production, with precision agriculture and environmental technologies included. A placement outside the university and a thesis are part of the degree. Graduates can start a crop or livestock business, or work in agricultural services, in banks assessing credit, or in insurance companies estimating damage.

name: Agricultural Water Management and Environmental Technology Engineering
overview: The curriculum mixes basic engineering, natural sciences, foundational agricultural studies, agricultural economics and professional subjects, with electives, a thesis and a period of professional practice. The focus is the way water problems sit inside wider environmental questions, together with the technical knowledge to deal with them. Graduates find work in agriculture, water management and environmental management, and the degree prepares you for a master's.

name: Food Engineering
overview: You combine biology, chemistry, physics, technical sciences and economics with specialist food science and food processing technology, choosing between compulsory courses and electives. A placement outside the university and a thesis complete the degree. Graduates work as laboratory managers, in quality assurance and auditing, or as product developers and production managers in food manufacturing. Other options include the pharmaceutical sector, animal feed production, regulatory authorities or a private food business, and a master's follows naturally.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: The programme covers financial and business management principles across finance, accounting, management, marketing and operations, and introduces financial technologies, data analytics and business intelligence tools. Graduates work as financial analysts, project managers, marketing coordinators, HR specialists or entrepreneurs, in areas from investment banking and consulting to marketing and human resources. The degree prepares you for a master's in business or finance.

name: International Business Economics
overview: You study micro- and macroeconomics, international freight, financial processes, economic policy and how the EU works, using IT and office automation tools to produce analyses and decision proposals in written and spoken form. Graduates take middle and senior management positions in domestic and international companies, and the diploma is recognised across the EU. A master's is the natural next step.

name: Tourism and Catering
overview: An economics core is combined with tourism and hospitality courses, optional vocational subjects and two foreign languages, with a project-oriented approach to teaching. In semesters seven and eight you complete a twelve-week professional placement each, at tourism or hospitality organisations, in the university's training restaurant and hotel, or through international partners, which also builds links with regional and international organisations. Graduates work in hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, regional organisations, local governments, museums and tourism marketing, as event organisers or in village tourism and gastronomy, and can continue to a master's.

name: International Relations
overview: The programme is multidisciplinary, drawing on international relations, history, economics, political science, foreign languages, sociology and regional studies, and it trains you to argue clearly in English. You finish with a thesis. Graduates are prepared for service in diplomatic, professional, business and academic communities, for example in a foreign service, as consultants for multilateral organisations or as development experts in non-governmental organisations.

name: Sociology
overview: You learn sociological theory, research methodology and social analysis, with practical and methodological skills built through the sociological research process, and the degree ends with a thesis. Graduates work in human resources, social and minority policy, education, health, urban management and development, regional development, media, marketing and public opinion research, environment and research management, for public bodies, companies, municipalities and NGOs. A master's is the next step for those who continue.

name: Recreation Management and Health Promotion
overview: The degree covers anatomy, physiology and exercise theory together with sports, health and organisational sciences. You take an active part in putting recreation and lifestyle programmes into practice and learn to teach sport and other recreational activities using adaptable learning strategies. Graduates work as organisers, instructors and consultants in sports organisations, healthcare, social and educational institutions, business services and civil organisations, designing tailored exercise programmes for settings such as wellness hotels and workplaces.

name: Nursing and Patient Care (Nurse specialization)
overview: The first year is built on anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, cell biology and histology, molecular biology and genetics, microbiology, public health and epidemiology. Later semesters turn to nursing in internal medicine, surgery and trauma, obstetrics, anaesthesiology, paediatrics, neurology, psychiatry, community care and oncology. Lectures are paired with clinical practice at the Petz Aladar County Teaching Hospital, and the final year centres on practice and a thesis you defend. Graduates work on hospital wards and intensive care, in outpatient care, general practice, hospices and care homes, or in healthcare centres, clinical research and pharmaceutical companies.

name: General Medicine
overview: The first two years lay the foundation of basic medical knowledge, and from the third year onwards regular clinical practice is added, with students working in the clinical departments of the teaching hospitals and treating patients under the supervision of physicians. The faculty's scientific laboratories also offer opportunities to get involved in research. In the final two semesters you rotate through the different medical specialties.

name: Dental Medicine
overview: The first two years teach the basic sciences of medicine and dentistry. Year three turns to dental diseases and their treatment, with preclinical modules such as restorative dentistry and prosthetic and oral surgery propedeutics, and you practise manual skills on phantom heads in the training laboratory. In years four and five you treat patients under continuous professional supervision, working more and more independently, with elective programmes in the final year. Graduates can apply for hospital residency positions, and EU citizens receive their licence automatically within the Community.

name: Pharmacy
overview: The programme begins with an introduction to the basic sciences and moves on to general and specialised pharmaceutical education. Training takes place across university departments, teaching pharmacies, institutes, hospitals and clinical pharmacies, laboratories and pharmaceutical works, so you see the profession in several settings. Graduates usually build careers at pharmaceutical or chemical companies, in laboratories or in hospitals.

name: Nurse
overview: You start with anatomy and physiology and move on to internal medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics and intensive care, with further courses in psychological care, nursing research, nursing management and counselling. Lectures and demonstration classes in the classroom are combined with clinical practice that begins after the first year, and the last two semesters are mainly field practice in clinics. The degree is equivalent to nursing degrees from other EU countries.

name: Physiotherapist
overview: You first learn how the human body works, in health and in disease, along with the theoretical and practical foundations of physiotherapy techniques. Later the focus shifts to clinical use: physiotherapeutic examination skills and treatment procedures, including more complex therapeutic methods. Teaching is in small groups using a problem-oriented approach, with clinical practice. Graduates work in prevention, healthcare and rehabilitation, either independently or as part of a healing team, with a focus on musculoskeletal conditions.

name: Psychology
overview: The programme covers developmental, cognitive, social and personality psychology, and treats research methodology as a central strand, following the research process from planning to data analysis. You carry out independent mini-research projects in the methodology courses and write a thesis in seminars, and a career socialisation course builds communication skills and professional identity. Graduates can work in areas such as commerce, finance, sport and entertainment, and the degree is a base for a master's in psychology, or in pedagogy and andragogy.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: The first semesters cover calculus, informatics, principles of economics, management, marketing, micro- and macroeconomics, business law, statistics, accounting and finance, with strategic management, operations management, human resource management and management control later on. Optional courses range from business ethics and negotiation skills to international finance, innovation, logistics, e-commerce and SAP. Teaching mixes theory with hands-on practice, and the final semester is a twelve-week internship at a company or non-profit organisation alongside the degree thesis. The programme trains managers who can work across economic sectors.

name: Tourism and Catering
overview: The programme looks at tourism and hospitality as both a business and a field of theory, with attention to current industry trends and the digital and online tools now used to sell and run tourism. Leadership, regional and local marketing, country image and brand building are named themes. Degrees of this kind typically start from economics, management, marketing and accounting and add courses on tourism products and hospitality operations. Graduates usually go into hotels, restaurants, travel companies, destination marketing and regional tourism organisations.

name: Computer Science
overview: The programme trains you to create, develop, implement, operate and service IT systems, working alone and in teams. Degrees of this kind typically begin with programming, discrete mathematics, calculus, algorithms and data structures, then move on to computer architecture, operating systems, databases, networks and software engineering, and end with a thesis project. Graduates usually go into software development, systems administration and other IT roles, or on to a master's in computer science.

name: Biochemical Engineer
overview: The programme pairs a theoretical basis with hands-on practice and includes an internship at a multinational or local company or a non-profit organisation. It trains bioengineers who apply biology in industry and applied science. Degrees of this kind typically cover chemistry, biology, biochemistry, microbiology and genetics, then bioprocess and engineering subjects, with substantial laboratory work and a thesis. Graduates usually work in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, food and chemical industries or continue to a master's.

name: Agricultural Engineering
overview: You study botany, zoology, mathematics, economics, business law, international agriculture and safety at work, then professional subjects such as crop production, horticulture, plant protection, animal husbandry, animal nutrition and health, and farm business management. Practical work covers soil preparation, nutrient supply, seeding, plant protection and harvesting, and you choose from four options: agricultural economics, animal production, horticulture and plant production. The final semester is an internship at an agricultural company. Graduates work in agriculture and agribusiness, in production and management, or in companies that process and market agricultural products.

name: English and American Studies
overview: You study the cultures, societies, history, language and literatures of the UK and the US, starting with intensive English language training and introductory courses in literature, culture and linguistics. Applied subjects include academic English and composition, sociolinguistics and second language acquisition. There are tracks focused on English or American literature, culture and history, a required minor in Hungarian and Central European Studies or in French, Italian, German or Spanish studies, and a BA thesis. Graduates go into cultural and public administration, tourism, international business, teaching, translation, journalism, diplomacy and the media.

name: Performance - Cello
overview: You study the cello as your main subject, working on solo playing and on playing in a symphony or chamber orchestra. Alongside it come solfege, chamber music, choir singing, piano accompaniment and sight-reading, plus theory subjects such as acoustics, art history, aesthetics, philosophy, ethics, music history, folk music and music theory. Graduates can work as soloists or members of symphony or chamber orchestras, or continue to a master's at the same faculty.

name: Performance - Clarinet
overview: You study the clarinet as your main subject, working on solo playing and on playing in a symphony or chamber orchestra. Alongside it come solfege, chamber music, choir singing, piano accompaniment and sight-reading, plus theory subjects such as acoustics, art history, aesthetics, philosophy, ethics, music history, folk music and music theory. Graduates can work as soloists or members of symphony or chamber orchestras, or continue to a master's at the same faculty.

name: Performance - Classical Singing
overview: You study classical singing as your main subject, working on solo performance and on singing and playing in chamber and symphonic settings. Alongside it come solfege, chamber music, choir singing, piano accompaniment and sight-reading, plus theory subjects such as acoustics, art history, aesthetics, philosophy, ethics, music history, folk music and music theory. Graduates can work as soloists or members of symphony or chamber ensembles, or continue to a master's at the same faculty.

name: Performance - Flute
overview: You study the flute as your main subject, working on solo playing and on playing in a symphony or chamber orchestra. overview: You study the violin as your main subject, working on solo playing and on playing in a symphony or chamber orchestra. Graduates can work as soloists or members of symphony or chamber orchestras, or continue to a master's at the same faculty.

name: Medicine
overview: The first two years cover foundation sciences such as anatomy, biochemistry and physiology, together with Hungarian language. Year three adds pathology, immunology and microbiology with introductory clinical subjects, year four brings surgery, internal medicine, pharmacology and radiology, and year five covers dermatology, neurology, psychiatry and family medicine, with thesis work. In the final year you care for patients in the departments of internal medicine, surgery, gynaecology, neurology, psychiatry and paediatrics. From the third year you also learn basic Hungarian to speak with patients. Graduates continue to specialist medical training or a PhD school.

name: Dentistry
overview: Year one covers biophysics, biostatistics, medical chemistry and oral anatomy, year two adds biochemistry, dental physiology and an introduction to prosthodontics, and year three brings clinical pathology, microbiology and propedeutics in restorative dentistry and oral surgery. In years four and five you work in complex dentistry, oral surgery, orthodontics, periodontology and paediatric dentistry, finishing with a thesis. Lab classes start in the first year, and manual techniques are developed through clinical training that balances theory with intensive practice.

name: Pharmacy
overview: Year one covers general chemistry, mathematics, physics and biophysics, pharmaceutical biology, Latin and Hungarian. Years two and three introduce pharmaceutical chemistry, technology and analytical methods, and the last two years turn to clinical applications such as clinical pharmacology, clinical pharmacy and pharmacovigilance, with topics like radiopharmacy and pharmaceutical management along the way. Graduates work in public and hospital pharmacies, laboratories, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, government agencies and health maintenance organisations, and some continue to doctoral research.

name: Nursing
overview: Year one covers the general principles of healthcare and nursing, biophysics and imaging diagnostics, with anatomy, biochemistry, psychology, microbiology and pathology. Year two brings internal medicine, pharmacology, paediatrics and skills development, and year three covers psychiatry, surgery, neurology, gynaecology and obstetrics. In year four you study anaesthesiology and intensive care, emergency care and rehabilitation, and write a thesis. More than half the curriculum is practical training, including a long internship in healthcare facilities. Graduates work in hospitals, clinics, nursing homes and rehabilitation centres, and can continue to doctoral programmes.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: Year one covers anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and the basics of physiotherapy, including electro-, balneo-, hydro- and climatotherapy. Year two adds clinical propedeutics and applied training methods, with techniques such as mobilisation and manual therapy. In year three you study internal medicine, neurology and orthopaedics for physiotherapists and the physiotherapy of the movement system, and year four covers intensive therapy and rehabilitation, with clinical placements in neurology, orthopaedics and rheumatology and a thesis. A compulsory internship is built in. Graduates work in therapy and rehabilitation services, balneotherapy institutions, home care, private practice and prevention.

name: Public Health
overview: Year one covers cell biology, anatomy, physiology, biostatistics and an introduction to public health, followed by epidemiology, immunology, microbiology and environmental topics. The later years apply this to occupational health, child and adolescent health, health promotion and health policy. Field work and laboratory practice sit beside the theory, and an internship is part of the degree. Graduates work in public health agencies such as cancer registries, food safety authorities and screening programmes, in community development and international aid, or in the pharmaceutical industry and management consultancies.

name: Agricultural Engineering
overview: Year one covers zoology, agricultural botany and chemistry, mathematics, informatics, animal physiology, soil science and water management. Year two adds land use, agricultural machinery, crop production, agroecology, animal husbandry and horticulture, and year three covers plant genetics and breeding, animal health, food technologies, quality management, farm business, forestry and integrated plant protection. The final semester is a twelve-week professional internship plus thesis work. Graduates work in agricultural enterprises, including management, in advisory and administration, in research institutes, on their own farms and in advocacy organisations.

name: Biochemical Engineering
overview: Year one covers mathematics, physics, general and organic chemistry, cell biology, microbiology and mechanical engineering. Year two moves into biochemistry, molecular biology methods, unit operations, bioprocess engineering, microbial physiology and genetics, and year three adds bioinformatics, analytical chemistry, plant biochemistry and spectroscopy. The last year covers quality management, safety and a thesis. A six-week placement at a company or research institute is part of the degree. Graduates can choose among careers across biotechnology, in research and development or in more practical roles.

name: Chemical Engineering
overview: After mathematics, physics, general, inorganic and organic chemistry in year one, you study physical and colloid chemistry, unit operations, process control, macromolecular chemistry and chemical technology. Year three adds qualitative and quantitative analysis, instrumental methods, plastics and processing, computer modelling of chemical technology systems, environmental technology and pilot plant work. Hands-on laboratory courses run alongside the theory, with a six-week internship at a company or research institute, and the last year covers safety and a thesis. Graduates can go on to master's programmes in chemistry, chemical, materials, environmental or bioengineering, or to a PhD in chemistry.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: Year one covers mathematics, physics, technical drawing, CAD modelling, mechanics, hydraulics, construction materials and geoinformatics. Year two adds hydrology, geology, geotechnics, transportation engineering and GIS, and year three covers water management, building construction, construction management, reinforced concrete, steel, timber and masonry structures and finite element modelling. The last year includes bridge design and a thesis project, and a six-week placement at a company or research institute is part of the degree. Graduates work as design, structural, building services and consulting or contracting civil engineers, construction managers and building control surveyors, or move into business and finance.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: You start with mathematics, physics, materials science, programming, electricity, measurements and electronics, then move to digital electronics, microelectronics, LabVIEW programming, circuit simulation and automation. Year three covers electronic technology, telecommunication, electric power systems and production management, and the last year adds enterprise economics and a thesis. A summer practice at an external professional institution is included. Graduates design, develop and maintain electrical control systems and components in engineering consultancies, manufacturing, automotive and railway engineering, steel manufacturing and water companies, working in multidisciplinary project teams.

name: Engineering Management
overview: The first years combine engineering foundations (mathematics, physics, mechanics, materials, electronics) with economics, accounting, quality management, project management, lean management, finance and law. In year three you choose one of three tracks: Construction, Industrial Process Engineering, or Material Handling and Logistics. A compulsory six-week practice and a thesis finish the degree. Graduates work as project, operations, supply chain, engineering and production managers, and can continue to a master's.

name: Environmental Engineering
overview: Year one covers mathematics, chemistry, applied biology, ecology and engineering informatics. Later years bring environmental techniques, noise control, waste management, air quality, soil management and monitoring, then environmental law, radiation protection, water environment protection, impact assessment and GIS, and finally environmental economics, project management and complex planning. A compulsory six-week internship at a company is included, and the thesis spans the last two years. Graduates work in industry on sustainable practice, emissions and waste, in government on environmental policy and regulation, and in research and consultancy on environmental technologies and impact assessments.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The first year covers mathematics, engineering physics, statics, materials engineering, technical drawing and CAD, and the second adds strength of materials, thermodynamics, dynamics and vibration, machine elements, measurement technology and fluid mechanics. In the second half you choose a track: Automotive Production Process Control, Building Services Engineering, or Operation and Maintenance. A compulsory six-week practice at a production company is included, along with a thesis. Graduates work in the automotive, chemicals, construction, metals, oil and gas, power generation, rail and utilities industries.

name: Mechatronics Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, engineering physics, electromagnetism, electronics and materials engineering, then mechanical machines, manufacturing technologies, mechatronic devices, measurement and data acquisition, pneumatics and hydraulics. Later subjects include electropneumatics, robots and robotic technology, electrical machines and drives, thermodynamic processes and cyber-physical systems, ending in a mechatronics project and thesis. Practical training runs throughout, with a compulsory six-week practice at a production company. Graduates work in robotics, automation, aircraft engineering, biomedical systems, transport and computer-aided design.

name: Vehicle Engineering
overview: The programme covers design and manufacturing, control systems and modelling, with significant emphasis on practical training and a compulsory six-week professional practice. In the latter half you choose a track: Vehicle Manufacturing, Automotive Vehicle Engineering, or Aircraft Engineering. A thesis completes the degree. Graduates work across transportation and manufacturing in the design, production and maintenance of automotive, railway, naval and aircraft systems, in mobile machinery, construction equipment and power management, and can continue to a master's.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: Year one covers mathematics, business informatics, economics, finance, communication, financial accounting, organisational behaviour and business law, followed by macroeconomics, corporate finance, marketing, international economics and statistics. Year three adds human resource management, controlling, EU studies, project management, entrepreneurship, decision theory and international business. The final semester is a mandatory internship and the thesis. Graduates work as human resources officers, marketing and sales executives, logistics and distribution managers and similar roles, and can move on to a master's.

name: Commerce and Marketing
overview: Year one covers economics, marketing basics, accounting, business law, EU studies and statistics, then management, corporate finance, marketing research, foreign trade and business planning. Year three adds enterprise resource planning systems, trade economics, brand management, pricing, services marketing, marketing channels, international marketing and advertising. A semester-long practice at a multinational or local company or non-profit organisation and a thesis close the degree. Graduates work in advertising, public relations, account and brand management, marketing and sales, and can continue to a master's and later a PhD.

name: Business Informatics
overview: The degree combines business and IT: management, business law, microeconomics and accounting alongside programming, operating systems and data management in year one. Year two adds finance, marketing, databases and business intelligence in practice, and year three covers software development and testing, SAP training, big data analytics and data visualisation. The last year includes data security, digital marketing and the foundations of artificial intelligence. An eight-week internship, at the university on research projects or at a company, and a thesis complete it. Graduates work as business analysts, system administrators and business data system developers.

name: Computer Science
overview: Year one covers discrete mathematics, programming, operating systems, calculus, databases, data structures and algorithms and cloud computing. Year two adds high-level programming languages, web technologies, applied statistics, software engineering and the foundations of artificial intelligence, with machine learning, image processing and game development. Year three covers web application development, software testing and data security, and a thesis. You apply the theory in an eight-week internship at the university on research projects or at a company. Graduates usually start as junior software developers, building mobile, desktop, web and multimedia applications, and can continue to a master's.

name: Computer Science Engineering
overview: Year one covers programming, electronics, physics, calculus, data structures, digital design and computer architectures. Year two adds networks, operating systems, control systems, software development, enterprise systems, web solutions and microcontrollers, and year three covers artificial intelligence, embedded systems, databases, IT security, computer graphics and telecommunication systems. The last year includes sensors and actuators and a thesis, and an eight-week internship at the university or a company is required. Graduates work as system designers, programmers, software and database developers, web designers and system administrators in production, services, banking, commerce and the civil service.

name: Biology
overview: Year one covers biological chemistry, the fundamentals of biology, plant and animal taxonomy, microbiology and ecology. Year two adds cell biology, plant and animal physiology, genetics, molecular biology and bioinformatics, and year three covers human biology, evolutionary biology, population genetics and a thesis. Hands-on experience is built in, including a six-week practice at a company or research institute. Graduates can continue to master's programmes in molecular biology, biology, bioengineering or environmental science, or work in research laboratories, schools, hospitals, environmental agencies and pharmaceutical, food, agricultural and chemical companies.

name: Biotechnology
overview: Year one covers physics, general, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, mathematics, cell biology, microbiology and genetics, with courses in communication and bioethics. Year two adds analytical chemistry, biophysics, bioinformatics, biochemistry, immunology, molecular biology and industrial and environmental biotechnology, and year three covers systems biology, bioanalytics, synthetic biology and pharmaceutical, medical, agricultural and food biotechnology, plus a thesis. Laboratory work runs throughout, with a six-week internship at a company or research institute. Graduates work in pharmaceutical, food, agricultural and chemical companies, research institutes and hospitals, or continue to a master's.

name: Chemistry
overview: Year one combines mathematics, physics, general, inorganic and organic chemistry, environmental science, chemical informatics, nuclear chemistry and a physical chemistry laboratory. Year two covers analytical and physical chemistry, separation techniques, spectroscopy, colloid chemistry and chemical technology, and year three adds quality management, biochemistry, environmental chemistry and technology, visits to chemical companies and a thesis. A six-week practice at a company or research institute is included. Graduates can take up entry-level jobs as chemists, clinical laboratory technologists or materials scientists, or continue to a master's in chemistry, chemical engineering or molecular biology.

name: Earth Sciences
overview: Year one covers mathematics, physics, mineralogy and geology, biology, chemistry, historical geology, physical geography, soil geography and ecology, along with earth sciences fieldwork. Year two adds structural geology, cartography, biogeography, hydrology, hydrogeology and climate studies, and year three covers geothermics, surface analyses and a thesis. You also complete a short practice at an external company, institution, university or research laboratory. Graduates work in environmental protection, resource management and geological surveying, or continue to a master's.

name: Mathematics
overview: Year one builds the basics: algebra and numbers, linear algebra, combinatorics and graph theory, geometry and analysis. Year two adds advanced algebra, number theory, multivariable calculus, computational geometry, linear programming, measure theory and numerical analysis, and year three covers differential equations, differential geometry, probability theory, cryptography, economic mathematics, optimisation and statistics, with a thesis. The programme balances theory with applications in computer science and physics. Graduates can work in government, teaching or industry, or continue to a master's in mathematics, applied mathematics or software engineering.

name: Physics
overview: Year one covers mathematics for physics, mechanics, thermodynamics, optics, calculus and linear algebra, with laboratory practicals alongside. Year two adds electromagnetism, condensed matter, quantum physics, differential equations and statistics, and year three covers quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical physics, fundamental interactions and a thesis project. A six-week practice at an external company or institution is required. Graduates work in quality assurance, environmental protection and materials science, or move on to postgraduate study in physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, informatics or economics.

name: Communication and Media Studies
overview: You study communication and media theory, media culture, film industry, scriptwriting, media law, ethics and economics in year one, then media text analysis, a media lab, strategic communication and marketing, and later press and media relations, news editing, press photography, radio and television studio training and creative writing. A journalism track is available, a 120-hour internship in editorial or corporate settings runs in the fifth semester, and a thesis completes the degree. Graduates work as journalists and broadcasters, in audiovisual content creation, public relations and social media management.

name: English and American Studies
overview: Year one builds language skills in reading, writing, speaking and listening, with grammar, pronunciation and British and American civilisation. Year two adds applied linguistics, American and British literature and culture, visual culture and the history of the USA and the British Isles. After the first year you choose a four-semester specialisation, then a two-semester track in year three, among Business English, English-Hungarian Translation, a minor in another programme, British Literature and Culture, Linguistics and Communication, and North American Studies. Graduates work in business and government, media, publishing, tourism and diplomacy, or continue to an English Studies or American Studies master's.

name: Psychology
overview: Year one covers the history of philosophy, communication theory, biology basics, statistics, and experimental, developmental, personality and social psychology. Year two adds research methodology, evolutionary psychology, personality diagnostics, sport, work and clinical child psychology, and year three has individual research projects, psychophysiology, psycholinguistics, helping relations, clinical and health psychology and a thesis. Graduates work as human behaviour analysts in recruitment, education and health organisations, assisting school or organisational psychologists or laboratory researchers under the supervision of a qualified psychologist, and the degree is a base for any psychology master's.

name: Classical Performing Arts (Music)
overview: You study technique and performance in your chosen instrument, voice or conducting, alongside music history and theory, solfege, folk music, acoustics, philosophy, art history, repertoire studies, piano, methodology and stage practice. Orchestra or choir, chamber music and ensemble work balance theory with practice, and an internship is part of the curriculum. You can specialise in piano, organ, guitar, strings, recorder, woodwind, brass, percussion, singing or choral conducting. Graduates work in musical institutions, professional ensembles and roles that need music education, or continue to a master's specialisation.

name: Contemporary Music
overview: The curriculum covers the history of classical and popular music, folk music and arrangements, solfege, music theory and applied composition, with cultural history, philosophy, improvisation, orchestration and sound editing. It is rich in hands-on experience and teaches practical artistic methods and professional performance tools. You choose an instrument from piano, organ, guitar, strings, recorder, woodwind, brass or percussion, or choose singing or choral conducting. Graduates work in musical institutions, professional ensembles and roles that need music education, or continue to a master's specialisation.

name: Musical Creative Art and Musicology
overview: Music theory and solfege are the main subjects, supported by music history, folk music, philosophy, art history, acoustics, repertoire studies, choral conducting, transposing and score reading, composition, choir, piano and voice, with a thesis. The curriculum balances theoretical depth with practical knowledge and performing skills. Graduates work as music theoreticians or music assistants in music institutions and other jobs that need music education, helping to spread Hungarian and European music culture, and can continue to a master's specialisation.

name: Veterinary Medicine
overview: The first two preclinical years cover anatomy, histology, embryology, biology, chemistry, physics, zoology, physiology and biochemistry. The following three clinical and paraclinical years bring animal breeding, pathology, pharmacology, toxicology, microbiology, parasitology, animal nutrition, surgery, obstetrics, food hygiene, epizootology and state veterinary medicine. The eleventh semester is practical work at the faculty clinics and associated institutions, on field stations and state farms and with practising veterinarians, and you submit a thesis and take a state examination before graduating. Graduates work in veterinary clinics, exotic and wildlife work, government veterinary posts and research.

name: Research Zoology
overview: The master's trains zoological researchers, and in its last two years you carry out individual research projects and build scientific communication skills. A tutorial system helps you find a thesis topic, including at research laboratories abroad. Programmes of this kind typically cover animal biology, evolution, ecology, physiology and the research methods and statistics used to study wild and captive species. Graduates go on to doctoral studies, research institutions, businesses that need zoological expertise, public administration or nature conservation.

name: Piano
overview: Your main subject is the piano, taught in English through individual lessons, with group classes alongside. Around it sit the supporting studies that instrumental degrees of this kind typically include: solfege, music theory, music history and piano, with chamber music and accompaniment typically part of the mix. The six semesters build towards public performance of solo and ensemble repertoire. Graduates usually continue to a master's degree at the academy or move into orchestras, chamber groups, solo work and teaching.

name: Orchestral Conducting
overview: Orchestral conducting is the main subject, taught in English in the academy's six-semester BA. Programmes of this kind typically centre on score study and rehearsal technique for the symphonic repertoire, supported by ear training, harmony, music history and piano, with chances to work with ensembles in practice. Graduates usually continue to a master's in conducting, and careers lie with orchestras, opera and concert organisations and music education.

name: Choir Conducting
overview: Choral conducting is the main subject, taught in English in the academy's six-semester BA. Programmes of this kind typically combine conducting technique and score study with rehearsing and leading a choir, supported by ear training, harmony, vocal studies, music history and piano. Graduates usually continue to a master's in conducting, and careers lie with choirs, vocal ensembles, concert and opera organisations and music education.

name: Classical Singing
overview: Singing is your main subject, with individual voice lessons in English and group classes alongside. Voice degrees of this kind typically add solfege, music theory, music history, piano, language and diction work, and chamber or choral singing, and the six semesters build towards public performance of song and operatic repertoire. The BA is the foundation for master's tracks at the academy in opera or in oratorio and lied. Graduates usually continue to a master's before careers in opera, concert and ensemble singing and teaching.

name: Piano
note: One overview for the Instrumental Performance card (20 instrument paths); the per-instrument lines above are held as boilerplate.
overview: You choose one main instrument from twenty (keyboards, strings, woodwind and brass, harp, guitar, cimbalom or percussion) and study it in individual lessons taught in English, with group classes alongside. Around the main subject, bachelor's degrees in classical performance usually add solfège, music theory, music history and piano, with chamber music and, for orchestral instruments, orchestra. Over six semesters the work builds towards performing in public, solo and in ensembles. The BA leads on to the academy's four-semester master's.

name: Performance - Piano
note: One overview for the Music Performance card (10 paths); the per-instrument lines above are held as boilerplate.
overview: You choose a main instrument (cello, clarinet, flute, guitar, harp, piano, trombone, trumpet or violin) or classical singing, and work both on solo performance and on playing in symphony and chamber orchestras. Alongside the main subject come solfège, chamber music, choir singing, piano accompaniment and sight-reading. Theory runs through the degree as well, from acoustics, aesthetics and philosophy to art history, music history, folk music and music theory. Graduates perform as soloists or in symphony and chamber orchestras, or continue to a master's at the same faculty.
